The products of iota(s+t epsilon) use those first three moment sums, so E_m^2=iota(A) is the desired ideal, with independent w,z and zero annihilator. A two-dimensional perfect evolution algebra has independent squares and no nonzero square-zero element, whereas A is perfect and epsilon^2=0; hence minimum envelope dimension 3. Because D=E² is characteristic with canonical unit and radical line, B0 residue form is invariant under isomorphism and B1 radical coefficient changes by an overall scalar; T=B0^-1 B1 transforms by conjugacy/scaling, making tr(T)^2/tr(T²) intrinsic. Eigenvalues -(m+2)/(2m), -(m+1)/m, -3/2 yield I=2(3m+2)^2/(7m²+6m+4), derivative -4(3m+2)(5m-6)/(...)²<0 for m>=3, giving pairwise nonisomorphism. Independently simplified exact rational expressions symbolically. No all-envelope classification is claimed.
